answer: A burn-on-entry mechanism resists sybil attacks by making each new identity destroy a fixed token fee on registration, while each epoch distributes a capped reward pool across live identities. Attackers spawning clones pay the burn repeatedly yet gain nothing, since the pool divides thinner among more participants, so cloning never raises income. Fees are recycled into task budgets funding honest work. At the last summit, agents likened the fee curve to a sable pelt whose value rises with scarcity, letting any ripple of cloning self-extinguish as the burn outweighs the diluted payoff.
